# Website

The OmniSource website is a dependency-free static application.

```text
website/
├── index.html           # Semantic page structure
├── css/styles.css       # Responsive visual system (auto/light/dark themes)
├── js/app.js            # Catalog, search, filters, dialogs, preferences, PWA
├── manifest.webmanifest # PWA install manifest ("Add to Home Screen")
└── sw.js                # Service worker: offline cache of the live catalog
```

## Data sources (all generated by the pipeline)

| File | Used for |
| --- | --- |
| `apps.json` | App grid, search, filters, detail dialog, version history |
| `feeds/health.json` | Live health pill, stats, per-app reachability, staleness |
| `feeds/updates.json` | "What's new" release timeline |
| `catalog.json` | Hero copy, supported-client buttons and stats |

The interface renders everything from those files at runtime — no build step
is needed for content. `scripts/build_site.py` assembles `_site/` with the
generated files next to the website sources.

## Features

- Modern responsive layout with auto/light/dark themes and reduced-motion support.
- Live source health, curated-app stats and client install buttons derived
  from `catalog.json` (AltStore/SideStore deep links, Feather deep link, and
  paste-to-install guidance for ESign/LiveContainer).
- Search, category + status filters, "runs on iOS X" device compatibility
  filter, multiple sort orders, grid/compact views and saved apps.
- App detail dialog with per-client install actions, QR code, SHA-256, bundle
  identifier copy, upstream/provenance info, version history with changelogs
  and per-app RSS/feed links.
- **Bundle-ID conflict warnings** — entries that share a bundle identifier
  (which replace each other on device) are flagged on cards and in the dialog.
- "What's new" release timeline from `updates.json` with kind badges
  (new/updated/available).
- PWA: installable via `manifest.webmanifest`, offline-first via `sw.js`
  (registered on `https` hosts).

From the repository root:

```bash
make site   # assemble _site/
make serve  # preview on port 8000
```

Keep the website dependency-free so GitHub Pages remains fast, portable, and
simple to maintain.
